categories.main_business_segments: Under Armour operates primarily in four geographic segments: North America, EMEA (Europe, Middle East, and Africa), Asia-Pacific, and Latin America. The company develops, markets, and distributes branded performance apparel, footwear, and accessories for men, women, and youth. Apparel is the largest segment by revenue, followed by footwear and accessories. The company also has a 'Corporate Other' segment, which includes digital platforms and certain corporate functions.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Under Armour's core technologies focus on performance-enhancing materials and designs, such as HEATGEAR®, COLDGEAR®, HOVR®, UA Flow™, and UA RUSH™. The company emphasizes technical fabrications, moisture-wicking, temperature regulation, and advanced cushioning in footwear. Most products are developed internally but manufactured by third-party contract manufacturers using proprietary and advanced materials sourced from a limited number of pre-approved suppliers.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The company serves a broad range of customers, including national and regional sporting goods chains, specialty retailers, department stores, institutional athletic departments, teams, and direct consumers through its own retail and e-commerce channels. Its products target athletes at all levels and consumers with active lifestyles, with a focus on performance and athletic use but also appeal for casual wear.
categories.geographic_coverage: Under Armour has a global presence, with North America (primarily the United States and Canada) accounting for about 65% of net revenues. EMEA, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America collectively represent approximately 34% of revenues. The company operates retail stores and e-commerce platforms in key international markets and distributes products through a mix of direct operations, distributors, and licensees.
categories.supply_chain_position: Under Armour operates primarily as a downstream company, focusing on product design, marketing, and distribution. Manufacturing is outsourced to unaffiliated third-party contract manufacturers, with the company overseeing sourcing, quality assurance, and supply chain management. The company manages inventory and distribution but does not own or operate manufacturing facilities.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include driving growth in footwear, women's, direct-to-consumer, and digital businesses, as well as expanding wholesale distribution. The company emphasizes innovation in performance materials, sustainability, and digital engagement with consumers. R&D efforts focus on technical advancements in apparel and footwear, sustainable materials, and circular design principles, alongside investments in digital platforms and omni-channel capabilities.
categories.revenue_model: Under Armour generates revenue primarily through product sales in wholesale and direct-to-consumer channels, including owned retail stores and e-commerce. Wholesale accounted for 59% and direct-to-consumer for 38% of net revenues in fiscal 2023. Additional revenue streams include licensing (2%) and digital subscriptions/advertising from digital platforms.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include Nike, Adidas, Puma, and lululemon athletica, all of which have greater resources and global brand recognition. Under Armour differentiates itself through its focus on performance and technical innovation but faces intense competition from both global and regional brands, as well as private label offerings from retailers. The company is positioned as a premium performance brand but is smaller in scale compared to its largest competitors.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2023, Under Armour reported net revenues of $5.9 billion, a 3.1% increase over the prior year. The company had net income of $386.8 million and gross margin of 44.9%. Growth was driven by international markets and footwear, while North America and apparel saw slight declines. The company maintains a strong liquidity position with $711.9 million in cash and continues to invest in growth and operational efficiency.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Under Armour's value proposition centers on making athletes better through innovative, high-performance products engineered for comfort, mobility, and technical advantage. The brand emphasizes superior materials, fit, and technology, aiming to deliver tangible performance benefits. Its focus on authenticity, athlete endorsement, and technical differentiation sets it apart from non-performance and lifestyle brands.
